newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares hit new record, more highs ahead.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares hit new record, more highs ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at a new record high on Thursday, fuelled by the strong dollar and US market, with dealers seeing more moderate gains ahead.
"The way things are at the moment with bonds and the dollar we can expect more gains ahead, though probably of a more modest nature," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 1.62 point to hit a new all-time closing record high of 154.48. The last record of 152.90 was on February 7. Overall bourse turnover of was 1.578 billion crowns. The KFX March future rose 1.60 point to 153.75 with 410 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
The dealer said that A.P.Moeller's two constituent shares were the main engine pushing the KFX on Thursday.
The shipping group's D/S Svendborg rose 10,000 crowns to 276,500 and D/S 1912 climbed 7,000 crowns to 193,000, apparently on belief that the dollar would remain strong, he said.
ISS ISG.N rose two crowns to 179, continuing its steady climb since it shed its troubled U.S. subsidiary.
SAS climbed 3.50 to 84 crowns on reports that it could help form a new global airline alliance. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
